paragraphs: Here's the lesson, friend: when the LORD speaks through His prophet, take Him at His word. Elisha, the prophet known as the man of God, told the woman that the LORD had decreed a seven-year famine, and she did as he instructed (2 Kings 8:1-2). She and her household lived as foreigners in the land of the Philistines for seven years, and I think that cost her something real (2 Kings 8:2).

Now look at what that obedience led to. She came home and went to the king to appeal for her house and her land, and Gehazi, Elisha's servant, was telling the king how Elisha had brought the dead back to life (2 Kings 8:3, 5). The text doesn't say why the timing worked out that way, so I won't either, but the king ordered, "Restore all that was hers, along with all the proceeds of the field from the day that she left the country until now." (2 Kings 8:6). Her seven years away didn't cost her the harvests, and that's the part I want you to hold onto.

So what does that mean for you, baker? The LORD's word is worth taking seriously, even when acting on it costs you something. This passage shows one woman who acted on it and then saw her house, her land and her missed harvests restored (2 Kings 8:6). It doesn't promise every baker the same ending, so keep listening to what God says, and keep those ovens ready.
